item.title: backlog history default output shows oldest-first — most recent items should appear at top
item.intent: backlog history must display items newest-first so the most recent sprint is always the first row, matching user expectations for a history command.
item.description: cmd_backlog_history uses 'tail -n "$limit"' to get the last N lines of sprints.jsonl, which are the most recent items. However they are then piped into the printf loop without reversal, so the output is chronological (oldest of the batch at the top). Users expect 'history' to show the most recent item first, like git log or shell history.
steps: After the tail, pipe through 'tac' (Linux) or detect macOS and use 'tail -r' to reverse the output before the printf loop
Check for tac availability; fall back to: awk 'NR==1{print; next} {lines[NR]=$0} END{for(i=NR;i>1;i--) print lines[i]}'
Apply the reversal in both the limited and --all branches
Run shellcheck — confirm zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: backlog history (default) shows the most recent sprint at the top row
backlog history --all shows all items newest-first
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
